A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same virtual-node analysis and VNG framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original VN/VNG benchmark experiments, commute-time calculations, and PairNorm, attention, and backbone ablations in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices H–I, including revised entries in the backbone ablation.

M1.justification: The general local-update, VN-update, and combination procedure is retained. However, the simplified VNG instance in Equation 14 changes from mean(h_local) to mean(Qh_local). This is a limited revision to the stated model instance; the PDFs do not establish a change to the trained implementations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight benchmarks: Peptides-Func, Peptides-Struct, MNIST, CIFAR10, MalNet-Tiny, and the three OGB tasks. The commute-time, smoothing, and attention scenarios are also retained; no new dataset or task coverage is introduced.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched main and appendix tables, including the graph-transformer baselines, GPS projection, PairNorm, standard VN, and GCN/GatedGCN comparisons. The newly cited interleaving work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix E and v2 Appendix G retain the same splits, validation-based model selection, parameter budgets, hyperparameter searches, and tabulated configurations. The added GPS/projection hyperparameter paragraph supplies documentation without reporting a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Table 8 revises the peptide evidence in the existing GCN-versus-GatedGCN backbone ablation, including whether VNG improves GCN on Peptides-Func. The PairNorm, mean-addition/subtraction, commute-time, attention-projection, and cosine-distance analyses remain; relocating the smoothing experiments does not remove them.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four runs for the peptide benchmarks and ten for the other benchmark experiments, with the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting practice. Changed standard deviations in Table 8 are numerical updates, not a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 8 changes GCN+PE+VN/VNG Peptides-Func scores from 0.6562/0.6537 to 0.6732/0.6862, reversing the reported VNG effect from -0.38% to +1.93%. Peptides-Struct scores change from 0.2540/0.2497 to 0.2475/0.2456, with corresponding uncertainty updates. The main benchmark scores and all five figures' underlying content are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem C.1 and its proof extending the expressivity analysis to input embedding layers, and Proposition F.1 with a self-attention Jacobian derivation. It also extends the argument to original PairNorm and changes the VN adjacency self-entry from 0 to 1. These are substantive formal additions and revisions; the existing mixing definition, pooling results, and commute-time results are largely retained or relocated.

C1.justification: The headline scope narrows to oversquashing and node heterogeneity: oversmoothing disappears from the title, abstract, and conclusion and becomes an explicitly qualified auxiliary contribution in the introduction. Its substantive claims remain in the appendix, while the principal VNG and benchmark-performance claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly positions VNG between homogeneous VN and fully heterogeneous GTs because its analyzed sensitivity lacks dependence on the receiving node. It adds a sparsity-based explanation of computational efficiency and identifies comparisons of alternative VNG message-passing mechanisms as future work. The linear-setting limitation is emphasized more strongly.

D1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F add explicit GCN and GatedGCN realizations of VN/VNG. Appendix G.4 identifies the hyperparameter source for GPS and its projection, and Appendix G.2 adds graph-size summaries. Existing hardware and detailed hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yin and Zhong's interleaving work and explicitly credits it and the already cited Rosenbluth et al. for prior practical benefits of asynchronous local/global updates. It also expands discussion of GT locality biases. Most other reference changes update publication metadata rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: the main oversmoothing section moves to Appendix B, its proofs and pooling discussion become separate appendices, and the corresponding empirical comparison moves to Appendix H.1. The abstract, contribution framing, outline, and conclusion are revised, while the sensitivity discussion gains substantial explanatory material.

P2.justification: The existing five figures and nine tables are retained. Figure 1 is enlarged and repositioned, the OGB table becomes a wider standalone display, and the PairNorm table moves to the appendix. Ranking colors, title and heading typography, and page styling also change, without a substantial redesign of the displays themselves.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition, implementation documentation, and qualification of the linear oversmoothing analysis. However, its expanded mathematics introduces unresolved problems: Equation 14 adds Q while Proposition 4.2 and its proof omit it, and Theorem C.1's claimed even-dimensional nonrepresentable example is realizable under its own coefficient equations. With the main empirical evidence unchanged, these formal problems offset the explanatory gains enough that a reliable net quality judgment is not supported.
